rules: State changes only through scripts/features.py. One feature active at a time. passing is irreversible.

features.title: Monorepo with ledger and dispatch services
features.behavior: fairsettle/ contains ledger/ and dispatch/ services, plus empty agent/; both services' existing unit tests pass from their new location.

verification.command: test -d ledger/.mvn && test -f dispatch/package.json && test -d agent && (cd ledger && ./mvnw -q test) && (cd dispatch && npm test --silent)

features.title: Rules checked, sandbox reachable
features.behavior: Official rules read (mainland eligibility, prizes, pre-existing code policy, video length); PayPal Sandbox app created; access token fetched, order created, approved in browser and captured by hand with curl.

steps: Eligibility, prize, pre-existing-code and video-length rules noted in docs/progress.md
Sandbox client id/secret stored in .env (not committed)
curl: token -> create order -> browser approval with sandbox buyer -> capture returns COMPLETED

features.title: ADR: PayPal state mapping
features.behavior: docs/adr/paypal-state-mapping.md maps PayPal order/capture/refund states onto the ledger payment and refund state machines, including approved-not-captured, capture timeout (UNKNOWN path, query before resend) and webhook ordering.

steps: Every PayPal status the adapter can receive has a row in the mapping
Capture timeout path says: query, never resend blindly
Reviewed against ledger docs/state-machines

features.title: PayPal auth client
features.behavior: Client-credentials token is fetched, cached until shortly before expiry and refreshed on 401; startup fails when the configured base URL is not the sandbox.

features.title: Create PayPal order
features.behavior: POST /v1/payments with provider=paypal creates an Orders v2 order with a PayPal-Request-Id derived from the ledger operation; a retry with the same Idempotency-Key returns the same order and never creates a second one.

features.title: Approval return and capture
features.behavior: After buyer approval the payment moves to approved-not-captured, then capture moves it to succeeded and posts balanced ledger entries; capture is idempotent.

features.title: Capture timeout goes to UNKNOWN
features.behavior: A capture call that times out leaves the payment UNKNOWN; recovery queries PayPal and settles the state without issuing a second capture.

features.title: Refund by capture id
features.behavior: Full and partial refunds are issued against the stored capture id, respect the ledger's refund reservation limit, and are idempotent on retry.

features.title: Webhook verification and inbox
features.behavior: PayPal webhooks are verified through the verification API (webhook id from config), deduplicated by event id in the existing inbox; a failed or timed-out verification never posts to the ledger.

features.title: Webhook events posted
features.behavior: Capture-completed and refund-completed events update payment/refund state and ledger entries; out-of-order or duplicate events are rejected by the state machine without side effects.

features.title: Full ledger regression green
features.behavior: The whole ledger suite, including Stripe and integration tests, passes with the PayPal adapter in place.

features.title: M1: real sandbox payment and partial refund
features.behavior: Against the real PayPal Sandbox: create, approve in browser, capture, partial refund, both webhooks received; ledger entries balance.

steps: Payment and refund visible in the sandbox merchant account
Both webhooks arrived through ngrok or the deployed URL and were posted once
Ledger balance check passes; order id, capture id and refund id recorded in docs/progress.md

features.title: One compose for all services
features.behavior: Root docker-compose.yml starts separate Postgres and Redis for ledger and dispatch (no port clash), Kafka, ledger api and worker, dispatch; every service reports healthy.

verification.command: docker compose up -d --wait && curl -fsS localhost:8080/actuator/health && curl -fsS localhost:8081/actuator/health && curl -fsS -o /dev/null localhost:4000/graphql?query=%7B__typename%7D

features.title: Ledger contract for new endpoints
features.behavior: contracts/ledger-openapi.yaml describes the refund-proposal and liability endpoints (amounts in integer cents, basis points summing to 10000) and lints clean.

features.title: Dispatch checkout through the ledger
features.behavior: Creating an order calls ledger POST /v1/payments with an Idempotency-Key derived from the order id; a retried order creation never creates a second payment.

features.title: Payment result drives order state
features.behavior: Ledger merchant notifications mark the order paid or failed through the existing order state machine; duplicates and out-of-order notifications are ignored.

features.title: Liability accounts and allocation
features.behavior: A refund with a liability split posts the cost to restaurant, courier and platform accounts in basis points; the parts always sum to the refund, the sub-cent remainder goes to the platform.

features.title: Refund proposal API and review
features.behavior: POST refund proposal (idempotent on complaint id) enters the existing review queue; approval executes the refund with its liability split in one transaction; rejection changes nothing.

features.title: Agent clients against fixtures
features.behavior: Typed clients read order, transitions, courier timeline (dispatch GraphQL) and payment, refundable amount (ledger REST); recorded fixtures replay without live services.

features.title: Policy checks
features.behavior: All 7 hard rules from the PRD are pure functions with a test each; any failure escalates and never trims an amount into compliance.

features.title: Gather and decide
features.behavior: Evidence is gathered in parallel without the model; the model returns a schema-valid RefundDecision (one retry on invalid output, then escalate); evidence refs are checked against collected events.

features.title: Propose, pause, resume
features.behavior: A passing decision is submitted as a proposal; the graph pauses with state in Postgres; after a process restart, approval resumes the same thread without resubmitting.

features.title: Execute and trace
features.behavior: After approval the agent triggers execution through the ledger only; every run is traceable in Langfuse by complaint id.

features.title: M2: full chain with PayPal
features.behavior: Live run: order paid with PayPal, complaint submitted, proposal approved in the console, refund visible in the sandbox, ledger shows the cost on the liable party.

steps: Complaint id, proposal id, PayPal refund id recorded in docs/progress.md
Ledger shows the allocation entries for the liable party
Langfuse trace for the run opens and shows cited evidence

features.title: Proactive trigger
features.behavior: A dispatch delivery-failure event starts the same flow as a complaint, deduplicated per order.

features.title: Investigate node
features.behavior: When evidence is insufficient the model may call read-only tools, at most 3 steps, then must decide.

features.title: Evaluation suite
features.behavior: 10 PRD scenarios run 3 times each from fixtures; zero policy violations and decision accuracy of at least 0.9; results written to docs/eval-results.md.

features.title: Complaint UI
features.behavior: A Gradio page submits a complaint for an order and shows the proposal status and a link to its trace.

steps: Submit a complaint from the page and see the proposal appear in the ledger console
Status updates after approval without a page reload error

features.title: Deployed
features.behavior: All services run on a public host with sandbox credentials only; PayPal webhooks reach it.

steps: Health endpoints respond on the public URL
A sandbox payment's webhook arrives at the deployed ledger

features.title: README and architecture
features.behavior: English README: one-line pitch, demo GIF, architecture diagram, quick start, eval results, what was pre-existing vs built during the hackathon.

steps: Fresh clone on another machine starts with the quick start alone
No secrets in the repository (git log -p | grep checks)

features.title: Demo video
features.behavior: Video within the rules' length limit following the agreed shot list; uploaded and viewable without login.

steps: Opens in a private browser window
First 20 seconds state the problem and the who-pays twist

features.title: Submitted on Devpost
features.behavior: Devpost entry submitted with repo, video and project text; checked in a private window.

steps: Submission confirmation received
Video, repo and demo links all open from a private window
